claims.content: The Customer wants to place a bid on an auction item.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to place a bid on an auction item.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer places a bid on an auction item.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is ready to place a bid on a specific auction item.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has successfully placed a bid on the auction item.
in_scope_actions: Place a bid on an auction item

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has agreed to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement.
The Customer is signed in.
The Customer's account contains the required minimum information needed to bid.

The Customer initiates placing a bid on an auction item by clicking the 'QuickBid Now' button to place a single bid, or by selecting an amount and clicking the 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid' button.
The Customer selects an amount and clicks the 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid' button.
The system displays a 'Bid Confirmation Pop-up' stating the bid amount, bid type, and payment method, with 'Yes, Place SmartBid' and 'Cancel' buttons.
The Customer confirms the bid by clicking 'Yes, Place SmartBid' (or equivalent).
The system processes the bid, and the Customer remains on the product details page.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of selecting a bid amount from the dropdowns and clicking 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid', the Customer uses the QuickBid option (clicking 'QuickBid' under an item in the catalog/category list view, or clicking 'QuickBid Now' when the 'QuickBid Amount' field is set); the system places a single bid adding the stated increment to the last bid.

Diverges from Step 4: If overtime bidding is ON and the Customer's bid is placed within the time-extension window (e.g., five seconds before the scheduled end), the auction automatically extends by the configured duration (e.g., 20 seconds).

missing_aspects: Evidence supports the automatic extension mechanism but does not explicitly state that the system 'processes the bid' as part of this specific alternative flow description.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 1 (and from Alternative Flow Step 1 when QuickBid is used): Before allowing the bid, the system checks whether the Customer is signed in. If the Customer is not signed in, the bid is not processed and the system takes the Customer directly to the sign-in page. After the Customer completes sign-in, if the Customer has the required minimum information to bid, the system returns the Customer to the Product Details page of the item they initially tried to bid on (or to the catalog page when the attempt originated from a catalog QuickBid button).

Diverges from Step 2: While the bid confirmation pop-up is displayed, the Customer clicks the 'CANCEL' button instead of confirming the bid. Exit: the system does not place a bid and the use case terminates for this attempt.

Diverges from Step 1: If the Customer has unresolved (unpaid) auction winnings greater than 7 days old, the system will not allow the Customer to place a bid. Exit: the bid is blocked and the use case terminates for this attempt.

Diverges from Step 1: If the Customer is subject to the escalation policy (failed to pay more than three times in a twelve-month period, unless less than 10% of total winnings), the system prevents the Customer from bidding again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status. Exit: the bid is blocked and the use case terminates for this attempt; the Customer can bid again only after the Review Status is removed.

missing_aspects: Explicit confirmation that 'no bid is placed' or that the 'sign-in redirection ends this bid attempt'.

claims.content: The Customer's bid is successfully processed, and the Customer remains on the Product Details page of the auction item rather than being redirected to a confirmation or checkout page.
The system records the bid with a timestamp precise to 1/100th of a second.
The Item Bid History table on the Product Details Page updates to include the new bid entry with the bidder's Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User? status.
The system updates the 'Current High Bid' dynamically for all items without requiring a page refresh.
